newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Senior Zaire officers to go before tribunals.
newsitem.headline: Senior Zaire officers to go before tribunals.

text.p: Six senior Zairean army officers detained on various charges of desertion, rape and pillage have been singled out to appear in front of military tribunals, the government spokesman said on Friday night.
All six of the officers were serving in the Zairean army when it was routed from the east of the country by mainly Tutsi rebels led by Laurent Kabila.
Rebellious Zairean soldiers have left a trail of destruction in their wake after fleeing the fighting in the east, wreaking havoc on civilians and their property in at least three provinces.

In an effort to bring the ragged, ill-disciplined troops to heel the government spokesman, Koloni Longo, announced on state television that military magistrates had been appointed to serve on tribunals in six different towns close to the conflict zone.
He added that the province of Upper Zaire, which has seen some of the worst pillaging by mutinous troops, has been declared a disaster zone.
"Uncontrolled elements of the Zairean army have committed acts of vandalism and carried out exactions on the population," Koloni said.
"Given the level of damage, Upper Zaire has been declared a disaster zone and will benefit from the same level of attention as the other regions of the east."
Koloni also announced that special offices would be opened across the vast to hear complaints from victims of military indiscipline.
The six senior officers so far named and singled out for trial are charged with crimes ranging from rape and pillage to desertion and selling weapons.
The government has declared that it intends to launch a counter-offensive against Kabila and his mainly Tutsi rebels in the east of the vast country.
But many commentators say they doubt the ability of the ill-trained and poorly paid army to retake captured territory.
